title: Map and Set Tooling Check
description: Choose Map/Set for lookups and avoid object-key traps.

questions.explanation: Object keys are coerced to string, so `1` and `"1"` collide. The later write wins — `obj[1]` is `"b"`.

questions.prompt: `Map` with `map.set(1, "a"); map.set("1", "b")` keeps how many entries?
questions.explanation: `Map` keeps arbitrary keys distinct. Number `1` and string `"1"` are different keys, so size is 2.

questions.prompt: Building a `Set` from array A then checking membership for each element of B turns nested `includes` scans into roughly:
questions.explanation: Converting an array to a `Set` for repeated checks turns O(n·m) nested scans into O(n + m).

questions.prompt: Using a plain object as `seen[idObject] = true` when `idObject` is an object is risky because:

options.text: The key becomes `"[object Object]"` and different objects collide

questions.explanation: Object keys coerce: `seen[idObject]` becomes `seen["[object Object]"]`. Use `Map` for non-string keys.
